This is actually a very different Discovery call than most med spa owners you've spoken to.

## Overall Assessment

**This is not a "marketing agency" sale.**

You're selling a highly analytical physician who:
- Is a rheumatologist first, not an aesthetic entrepreneur.
- Has plenty of capital already invested.
- Is extremely skeptical.
- Hasn't even launched marketing yet.
- Wants to architect the business correctly from Day 1.
- Hates wasting money.
- Wants systems more than leads.
- Wants to understand your thinking before he'll ever trust you.

He isn't emotionally buying.

He's intellectually qualifying you.

Arlene actually did a decent job considering this was one of her first calls, but she missed the opportunity to uncover what is really driving him. fileciteturn0file0

---

# Biggest Things We Learned

### Current Situation

Dr. Aryo Alborz

• Rheumatologist for 16 years

• Existing practice in Turlock

• Brand new regenerative medicine / aesthetics clinic in Pleasanton

• Open only **2 weeks**

• Significant investment already made

Equipment includes:

- Potenza
- Pico laser
- DEKA laser
- BTL EmFace
- Emsculpt Neo
- Emsella
- Axion

He's already heavily invested.

He's not shopping because he lacks money.

He's shopping because he doesn't want to make expensive mistakes. fileciteturn0file0

---

# His Goals

This was the gold.

He wants to build a medical brand.

Not just a med spa.

He repeatedly said:

"I want to do things correctly from the beginning."

"I don't want trial and error."

"I only want one system."

"I don't want to switch CRMs."

"I don't want to waste money."

"I want to learn the pattern."

Those are his buying motives.

NOT LEADS.

---

# What He Actually Wants

He wants someone to become:

"The Chief Architect"

Not

"The Marketing Guy."

Huge difference.

---

# Biggest Pain Points

## 1. He doesn't trust marketing agencies.

He literally says:

> Everyone is an expert now.

He believes:

- agencies oversell
- nobody understands medicine
- everyone has opinions
- nobody has systems

You need to separate TLC from agencies almost immediately.

---

## 2. He wants ONE integrated operating system.

This is huge.

He doesn't want:

CRM A

Marketing B

Phone C

Automation D

Calendar E

AI F

He wants one ecosystem.

Your CRM conversation will resonate massively.

---

## 3. He needs staff.

Specifically:

RN

Medical Assistant

Eventually physicians

This means...

Generating 200 leads next month is actually BAD.

Because operations aren't ready.

---

## 4. He wants QUALITY.

He said something incredibly important.

> I'd rather have 25 perfect patients than 50 bad ones.

That sentence tells you everything.

He does NOT want Groupon Botox patients.

---

## 5. He wants premium positioning.

He spent almost five minutes talking about cheap Botox.

Why?

Because he wants to position himself ABOVE that.

That's exactly where Luxora should meet him.

---

# Biggest Opportunity

This is where I would completely pivot your Discovery.

Don't sell marketing.

Sell business architecture.

---

# What I Would Diagnose

By the end of Discovery I'd say something like:

> Raj...
>
> When we first spoke, you thought the biggest challenge was finding the right marketing strategy.
>
> After hearing everything today...
>
> I actually don't think marketing is your biggest problem.
>
> I think marketing is the LAST thing I'd focus on.

Pause.

Then continue.

>I think there are three much bigger bottlenecks.

---

## Bottleneck 1

No operational infrastructure.

No CRM

No patient journey

No automation

No follow-up

No memberships

No retention

No systems

---

## Bottleneck 2

No positioning.

He has incredible differentiation.

Rheumatology.

Regenerative medicine.

Autoimmune expertise.

Wellness.

TMJ.

Pain.

Stem cells.

Medical credibility.

Yet none of it has been translated into a market position.

That is actually what needs built.

---

## Bottleneck 3

No predictable acquisition engine.

Eventually you'll build ads.

But not before the first two.

---

# I'd Challenge Him

This is where I'd go much deeper than the script.

Raj...

You've mentioned multiple times that you don't want to make expensive mistakes.

Let me ask you this.

If I handed you 100 ideal patients next month...

Would you honestly want them walking into the business exactly as it exists today?

He'll almost certainly say no.

Then ask:

Why not?

Now he'll tell you the roadmap himself.

---

# I'd Explore This More

He said something that should become the center of the conversation.

>I want to learn the pattern.

Ask:

What does "learning the pattern" look like to you?

That's gold.

---

# Biggest Emotional Driver

He isn't buying revenue.

He's buying certainty.

That's the difference.

---

# His Buying Personality

I'd classify him as:

Engineer

Scientist

Architect

Very high analytical.

Very low emotional.

Very low urgency.

Very high trust threshold.

He'll likely make a great client...

once convinced.

---

# Biggest Mistake to Avoid

Do NOT sell:

More leads

Meta ads

Google ads

Facebook

Instagram

He doesn't care.

Yet.

---

Instead...

Sell:

Operating system

Patient journey

Infrastructure

Market positioning

Patient lifetime value

Medical brand strategy

Clinical differentiation

That's what he's actually buying.

---

# I Would Slightly Modify Your Transition

Instead of saying:

"Based on everything we've discussed..."

I'd say:

> Raj...
>
> I actually think you came to us asking the wrong question.
>
> You came looking for marketing.
>
> But after hearing your vision...
>
> I think what you're actually trying to build is an entire growth infrastructure.
>
> Marketing is simply one piece of that.

Pause.

> That's exactly why I think we're having this conversation.

That immediately reframes you from vendor to advisor.

---

# His Personalized Three Priorities

Instead of your standard recommendations, I'd make them these:

### Priority 1: Build the Foundation

- CRM
- patient journey
- automations
- follow-up
- workflows
- scheduling
- reporting

Before spending heavily on advertising.

---

### Priority 2: Position the Brand

Develop messaging around:

- Rheumatologist-led care
- Autoimmune expertise
- Regenerative medicine
- Wellness
- Premium outcomes
- Medical credibility

Differentiate him from "discount Botox clinics."

---

### Priority 3: Launch Predictable Acquisition

Only after the infrastructure exists.

Use Meta, Google, referral systems, reactivation, and retention to attract the *right* patients, not bargain shoppers.

---

# Biggest Objection You're Going to Get

Not price.

Documentation.

He literally asked:

> Send me your proposal.

He's looking for proof.

Not because he wants to avoid the meeting.

Because that's how physicians evaluate decisions.

Instead of resisting, lean into it. Send a concise pre-read that outlines your three-stage framework (Diagnose → Acquire → Create Lifetime Clients) and the agenda for the strategy session, but save the personalized diagnosis and recommendations for the call. That gives him enough structure to feel prepared without giving away the prescription before you've walked him through it.

---

# Closing Strategy

Your goal isn't to create urgency through scarcity.

Your goal is to create confidence.

When you present the recommendation, position it like this:

> Raj, based on everything you've shared, I wouldn't advise you to spend another dollar on aggressive marketing until we've built the infrastructure to support the kind of premium practice you want. The good news is that your vision and your clinical expertise give you an incredible foundation. Our job is to help you build the systems, positioning, and patient journey that allow that vision to scale predictably.

That language aligns directly with what he repeatedly told your team he values: doing it right the first time, avoiding costly mistakes, and building a premium practice rather than chasing volume. It also fits naturally into your existing Call 2 framework while making the recommendation feel like a physician-to-physician prescription rather than a sales presentation. fileciteturn0file0turn0file1
